narrative: The model estimated a 65% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that risk exceeded the threshold used for admission, your law school application was rejected. The denial therefore reflects a risk estimate driven mainly by the admission test score and third-year academic standing, with your undergraduate record offering some counterweight. Your gender and race were not used in this prediction. To improve your position, focus on raising your admission test score if you can retake it, address the third-year academic decline through additional coursework or an explanatory statement, and seek admissions counseling about schools or pathways that review applications more holistically. You may also ask whether you can submit updated scores or evidence of improved academic performance before reapplying.
